_meta.title: Qwen3.7 blog deep re-investigation — sections beyond the 41-bench table (YC-Bench, KernelBench speedup, robotics models)
_meta.context: Re-read of https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.7 + https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-7-max with focus on sections initially skipped. The first Qwen 3.7 ingest pass (Session 20 cont'd 2, commit f120612) captured only the 41-benchmark × 6-model comparison table at the top of the blog. The blog actually contains 15+ headings including case studies + new benchmarks + new robotics models, plus the AA page has a precise JSON-embedded AAII ranking. Deep-dive findings: (1) blog's 'Long-Horizon Planning and Execution in Startup Management' section introduces YC-Bench — full 1-year startup simulator with hundreds of decision rounds (personnel/contracts/malicious-clients), reports revenue + tasks-completed for 3 generations of Qwen Plus/Max models; (2) blog's 'Phyicial-World Navigation Agent' section introduces Qwen-RobotClaw (robotics agent harness) + Qwen-RobotNav (navigation foundation model) — quadruped robot dog control demo via tool-use; (3) KernelBench L3 cells 'x.xx/yy%' represent geomean-speedup + pass-rate dual metric — first ingest captured only pass-rate, this adds the speedup column; (4) AA model detail page JSON-embedded ranking confirms Qwen3.7-Max AAII=56.58 (rank 4, behind GPT-5.5 60.24 / Opus 4.7 57.28 / Gemini 3.1 Pro 57.18) — page text claim of 'scores 57' is the rounded value; existing aa_intelligence_index=57 ingest preserved per strict-attribution; (5) blog's 'Self-Evolving in the Wild' Extend Attention case study and 'Reward Hacking Monitoring' SWE-RL case study are reported as case-study narratives without bench-name labels — kept in seed_sources.yaml note but not ingested as scores per strict-attribution.
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION + PRESERVATION. YC-Bench revenue + tasks-completed are clearly labeled metrics in the blog with 3-model panel — clean ingest. KernelBench L3 speedup added as separate benchmark (kernelbench_l3_speedup) so existing kernelbench_l3 (pass-rate) entries are not duplicated. Qwen-RobotClaw + Qwen-RobotNav registered as new models but no scores ingested (only demo footage; no bench results). Qwen3.5-Plus newly registered (only YC-Bench score available). 'Self-Evolving' / 'Reward Hacking' / 'Cowork Productivity' case-study numbers (10.0x kernel speedup, 1,618 hacking cases) are point estimates of a single execution, not population benchmarks — recorded in seed_sources notes but not as scores.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 Plus
models._note: Historical Plus-tier model in the Qwen 3.x lineage. Surfaced as YC-Bench baseline in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog (5.9x lower revenue than 3.7-Max). Registered here only to attribute the YC-Bench score; capability coverage on other benches not added pending separate primary source.

models.name: Qwen-RobotClaw
models._note: Robotics agent harness for quadruped robot control. Demoed in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 'Physical-World Navigation Agent' section — operates a robot dog via tool-use calls for physical understanding + planning + memory + decision-making in physical environments. No public benchmark scores yet; demo only (20-minute first-person trajectory).

models.name: Qwen-RobotNav
models._note: Navigation foundation model for physical-world agents. Component of Qwen-RobotClaw harness. No public benchmark scores yet; companion to RobotClaw demo.

benchmarks.name: YC-Bench — Total Revenue (USD)
benchmarks.description: 1-year-lifecycle startup management simulator. Agent navigates hundreds of decision rounds covering personnel, contracts, malicious-client identification, and labor-cost management to maximize profit. Metric: total revenue (USD) at end of simulated year. Introduced in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20 within 'Long-Horizon Planning and Execution' section. Tests policy consistency across 1000+ step trajectories, resilience to context rot, strategic evolution.

benchmarks.name: YC-Bench — Tasks Completed
benchmarks.description: Companion metric to yc_bench_revenue — number of discrete tasks the agent successfully completed during the 1-year simulated startup lifecycle. Introduced in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: KernelBench L3 — Geomean Speedup
benchmarks.description: KernelBench Level-3 (composition of multiple CUDA primitives) — geometric mean speedup over PyTorch reference. Higher = better. Companion to kernelbench_l3 (pass-rate). Cells of form 'x.xx/yy%' in Qwen blog comparison panel represent dual metric; this records the geomean-speedup component.

scores._section: === YC-Bench (Qwen3.7-Max launch blog, 'Long-Horizon Planning and Execution' section) ===
scores._note: $2.08M total revenue — 2x Qwen3.6-Plus, 5.9x Qwen3.5-Plus. Successfully completed 237 tasks. Agent demonstrated strategic evolution: actively explored potential clients, identified+blacklisted malicious traps, prioritized reliable revenue streams, autonomously recovered from mid-term crises.
$352K — 5.9x lower than Qwen3.7-Max. Demonstrates Qwen 3.5 -> 3.6 -> 3.7 long-horizon planning improvement trajectory.

scores._section: === KernelBench L3 — geomean speedup component (companion to existing kernelbench_l3 pass-rate) ===
scores._note: 'Opus-4.6 Max' column. KernelBench L3 speedup #1 in panel + pass-rate #1 (98%). Pareto-optimal on this benchmark.
'GLM-5.1 Thinking' column. 2nd highest speedup despite lower pass-rate (78%).
'DS-V4-Pro Max' column. Lowest speedup in panel.
Geomean speedup paired with 96% pass-rate. Pareto-comparable to Opus 4.6 Max (2.63x / 98%) — Qwen3.7-Max trades some speedup for slightly lower pass-rate.
